collections.name: Studio Ghibli
collections.description: The complete 27-work official Studio Ghibli works list, including Nausicaä, On Your Mark and Ghiblies Episode 2.

collections.name: Kyoto Animation
collections.description: Emotion, character acting and some of television anime's finest compositing.

collections.name: Madhouse
collections.description: Decades of prestige, genre range and animator-driven productions.

collections.name: MAPPA
collections.description: Modern high-intensity studio work across action, drama and experimental originals.

collections.name: Bones
collections.description: Character animation, action and long-running genre craftsmanship.

collections.name: GAINAX → Trigger
collections.description: The maximalist lineage from Gainax experimentation to Trigger spectacle.

collections.name: ufotable
collections.description: Digital compositing, effects-heavy action and premium franchise filmmaking.

collections.name: Production I.G
collections.description: Cyberpunk, sports and grounded action with a long technical legacy.

collections.name: Science SARU
collections.description: Loose movement, formal experimentation and director-forward productions.

collections.name: WIT Studio
collections.description: High-end action and adventurous production design.

collections.name: SHAFT
collections.description: Graphic composition, dialogue-driven direction and a very recognizable visual grammar.

collections.name: Sunrise / Bandai Namco Filmworks
collections.description: Mecha, space opera and some of anime's most durable franchises.

collections.name: CloverWorks
collections.description: Polished character animation across romance, comedy and action.

collections.name: A-1 Pictures
collections.description: Mainstream range from romance to huge action productions.

collections.name: Toei Animation
collections.description: Foundational television anime and enduring mass-audience franchises.

collections.name: Studio 4°C
collections.description: Experimental features, anthologies and aggressively stylized animation.

collections.name: P.A.WORKS
collections.description: Workplace drama, original series and emotionally direct features.

collections.name: Orange
collections.description: The studio most responsible for proving character-driven CG anime can look fantastic.

collections.name: David Production
collections.description: Bold color, sound and adaptation choices.

collections.name: Pierrot
collections.description: Long-running shonen and several defining 80s-00s adaptations.

collections.name: TMS Entertainment
collections.description: Classic franchises and modern sports/drama hits.

collections.name: White Fox
collections.description: High-concept fantasy and time-loop drama.

collections.name: CoMix Wave Films / Makoto Shinkai
collections.description: Shinkai's evolving visual language from tiny digital shorts to global theatrical blockbusters.

collections.name: Satoshi Kon
collections.description: Kon's feature filmography plus Paranoia Agent.

collections.name: Mamoru Hosoda
collections.description: Digital worlds, family structures and kinetic feature animation.

collections.name: Masaaki Yuasa
collections.description: Elastic animation and formal invention across comedy, drama and music.

collections.name: Shinichiro Watanabe
collections.description: Music-driven genre hybrids with some of anime's best action direction.

collections.name: Mamoru Oshii
collections.description: Political, technological and philosophical animation with a singular sense of space.

collections.name: Naoko Yamada
collections.description: Micro-gesture character direction, music and emotionally precise filmmaking.

collections.name: J.C.STAFF
collections.description: A huge genre-spanning television catalog: romance, comedy, food battles, fantasy and some of the best Railgun material.

collections.name: Studio DEEN
collections.description: A long-running studio whose strongest work ranges from classic comedy and horror to adult drama and BL romance.

collections.name: Kinema Citrus
collections.description: Dense fantasy worlds, tactile backgrounds and emotionally direct character animation.

collections.name: Brain's Base
collections.description: An unusually strong run of ensemble drama, supernatural stories and character-first adaptations.

collections.name: Satelight
collections.description: Music, mecha and maximalist science fiction are the studio's natural habitat.

collections.name: Polygon Pictures
collections.description: A major Japanese CG studio, strongest when architecture, machinery and hostile futures are part of the appeal.

collections.name: OLM
collections.description: Far broader than Pokémon: sports, thrillers, comedy and several excellent modern adaptations sit in its catalog.

collections.name: Doga Kobo
collections.description: Character animation and comic timing, with recent work proving the studio can pivot into glossy high-stakes drama.

collections.name: SILVER LINK.
collections.description: A reliable home for colorful fantasy, comedy and character-driven television anime.

collections.name: LIDENFILMS
collections.description: A broad modern catalog with especially good recent work in nocturnal romance, historical action and grounded drama.

collections.name: TROYCA
collections.description: Director-forward originals and polished adaptations with a taste for adult drama, mystery and clean digital compositing.

collections.name: Lerche
collections.description: Visually assertive comedy, romance and school stories, often with darker material hiding behind a bright surface.

collections.name: Studio Colorido
collections.description: Compact features and shorts built around expressive color, youth stories and unusually fluid movement.

collections.name: Passione
collections.description: Ecchi, horror and fantasy handled with far more visual personality than the studio's niche reputation suggests.

collections.name: Sony Pictures Animation
collections.description: One of the central studios behind the current stylized-CG revolution in mainstream Western feature animation.

collections.name: Powerhouse Animation
collections.description: US adult/action animation with an openly anime-influenced visual vocabulary and excellent fight direction.

collections.name: Studio Mir
collections.description: A key bridge between Korean production craft and high-end Western action animation.

collections.name: Titmouse
collections.description: Adult serialized animation that ranges from cerebral sci-fi to fantasy comedy and alien ecology.

collections.name: Fortiche Production
collections.description: Painterly 2D/3D hybrid animation and cinematic character acting; the studio that made Arcane a visual benchmark.

collections.name: Studio Ponoc
collections.description: A Ghibli-descended feature studio with lavish hand-drawn fantasy and emotionally direct short-form work.

steps.note: Again use a filler guide; do not treat filler as required continuity.

steps.title: The Last: Naruto the Movie
steps.note: Watch after Shippuden episode 493 / before the final wedding stretch.

franchises.name: Bleach
franchises.summary: Original TV plus Thousand-Year Blood War.

steps.title: Bleach original series
steps.note: Skip anime-original filler arcs unless curious.

franchises.name: One Piece
franchises.summary: One continuous main story. Movies are optional; pacing is the main issue rather than continuity.

steps.title: One Piece TV from episode 1
steps.note: Use the official anime or a reputable filler/pacing guide; do not skip canon arcs for chronology.

steps.title: One Piece Fan Letter
steps.note: Best after you know the world/cast; it contains broad franchise context.

steps.title: Theatrical films
steps.note: Mostly standalone/non-canon; Film Z, Gold, Stampede and Red are the major modern spectacle picks.

franchises.name: Demon Slayer
franchises.summary: Film/TV duplication exists around Mugen Train. Pick one version.

steps.title: Mugen Train film OR Mugen Train TV arc
steps.note: Do not need both.

franchises.name: Made in Abyss
franchises.summary: One movie is mandatory; the recap films are not.

steps.title: Journey's Dawn / Wandering Twilight recap films
Season 2: The Golden City of the Scorching Sun

franchises.name: Puella Magi Madoka Magica
franchises.summary: TV series then Rebellion; recap films are optional.

steps.title: Walpurgisnacht: Rising
steps.note: Continue once released/available in your region.

franchises.name: Macross
franchises.summary: Shared history, but several entries can be enjoyed independently.

steps.title: Do You Remember Love?
steps.note: Film retelling/alternate version, worth seeing even after TV.

steps.title: Macross Zero
steps.note: Prequel, but better after some franchise context.

franchises.name: Fullmetal Alchemist
franchises.summary: 2003 and Brotherhood are separate adaptations. Neither is a season of the other.

franchises.name: Higurashi / When They Cry
franchises.summary: Do not start with Gou even though it initially looks like a remake.

steps.title: Higurashi Gou
steps.note: Sequel, not beginner remake.

franchises.name: Trigun
franchises.summary: Original and Stampede/Stargaze are separate interpretations.

franchises.name: Castlevania
franchises.summary: Nocturne is a later-generation sequel continuity.

franchises.name: Psycho-Pass
franchises.summary: Season 1 is the masterpiece, but the later continuity is navigable.

steps.title: Providence
steps.note: Release-later prequel material; best after Season 3 context.

franchises.name: GRIDMAN Universe
franchises.summary: Two TV series converge in the movie.

franchises.name: Avatar animated universe
franchises.summary: Straight chronological generations.

franchises.name: Spider-Verse
franchises.summary: Feature continuity.

steps.title: Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse
steps.note: Watch when released.

franchises.name: Violet Evergarden
franchises.summary: Release order works, but the Extra Episode has a precise chronological slot between TV episodes 4 and 5.

steps.title: Violet Evergarden Special / Extra Episode
steps.note: Chronologically between TV episodes 4 and 5.

steps.title: Eternity and the Auto Memory Doll

franchises.name: Attack on Titan
franchises.summary: The main television story is linear; the OVAs are optional side material and are safest once the relevant characters have been introduced.

steps.title: Attack on Titan OVA
steps.note: Episodes 1-3: Ilse's Notebook / A Sudden Visitor / Distress.

steps.title: Attack on Titan: No Regrets
steps.note: Episodes 1-2. Levi prequel; better once you know him.

steps.title: Attack on Titan: Lost Girls
steps.note: Episodes 1-2: Wall Sina, Goodbye.

steps.title: Attack on Titan: Lost Girls
steps.note: Episode 3: Lost in the Cruel World.

franchises.name: Code Geass
franchises.summary: The original TV ending and the recap-film continuity are not exactly the same timeline. Resurrection follows the films.

steps.title: Code Geass: Lelouch of the Rebellion
Lelouch of the Re;surrection
steps.note: This sequel follows the recap-film changes, not the exact TV ending.

franchises.name: Hellsing
franchises.summary: Ultimate is the complete manga-faithful route. The 2001 TV series becomes its own story.

steps.title: Hellsing (2001) episodes 1-13
steps.note: Interesting atmosphere and music, but increasingly anime-original.

franchises.name: Legend of the Galactic Heroes
franchises.summary: The classic OVA and Die Neue These are separate adaptations. The two classic films make a particularly clean entrance into the OVA.

steps.title: My Conquest Is the Sea of Stars
Overture to a New War
steps.note: Expanded retelling of the OVA opening; after this start the main OVA at episode 3.

steps.title: Legend of the Galactic Heroes OVA episodes 3-110
Gaiden prequel stories
steps.note: Chronologically earlier, but better after the main story.

steps.title: Legend of the Galactic Heroes: Die Neue These

franchises.name: Blue Exorcist
franchises.summary: Season 1 diverges into an anime-original ending. For a clean canon route, jump away before those episodes.

steps.title: Season 1 episodes 18-25
steps.note: Anime-original continuity; later canon seasons ignore it.

franchises.name: Black Butler
franchises.summary: The early anime contains major anime-original blocks. The manga-canon route requires explicit episode jumps.

steps.title: Season 1 episodes 13-15
steps.note: Episode 15 contains some anime-original material near the end, but this is the relevant adapted arc.

steps.title: Season 1 episodes 16-24 + all of Black Butler II

franchises.name: The Promised Neverland
franchises.summary: Season 1 is excellent. The second anime season compresses and removes too much material to be the recommended continuation.

steps.title: Continue with the manga from chapter 38
The Promised Neverland Season 2
steps.note: Watch only out of curiosity after knowing what was cut.

franchises.name: The Garden of Sinners / Kara no Kyoukai
franchises.summary: The movies are intentionally nonlinear. First-time viewers should use release order rather than trying to repair the chronology.

franchises.name: Sword Art Online
franchises.summary: Progressive is a parallel Aincrad retelling, not the next season. Ordinal Scale belongs between SAO II and Alicization.

steps.title: Progressive: Aria of a Starless Night

franchises.name: Re:ZERO
franchises.summary: The Director's Cut can replace the original first season; do not watch both unless you want comparisons.

steps.title: The Frozen Bond
steps.note: Prequel material, best after meeting Emilia and Puck.

franchises.name: Mushoku Tensei
franchises.summary: Mostly linear; the Eris OVA fills a gap inside the first season but works well immediately after it.

steps.title: Eris the Goblin Slayer OVA
steps.note: Takes place during the first-season journey; watch after Season 1 to preserve flow.

franchises.name: KONOSUBA
franchises.summary: The Megumin spinoff is chronologically earlier, but it plays better after you already know the main cast.

steps.title: An Explosion on This Wonderful World!
steps.note: Megumin prequel.

franchises.name: Clannad
franchises.summary: After Story is the main continuation. The Tomoyo and Kyou chapters are alternate-route bonus episodes, not branches you need to splice into the main continuity.

franchises.name: Fruits Basket (2019)
franchises.summary: The 2019 adaptation is one continuous complete route. Prelude is best left until the ending is known.

steps.title: Fruits Basket: Prelude
steps.note: Contains recap plus additional prequel/epilogue material; safest after The Final.

franchises.name: Rurouni Kenshin
franchises.summary: The 1996 series and 2023 remake are separate adaptations. Trust & Betrayal is an acclaimed prequel OVA that works after you know Kenshin.

steps.title: Rurouni Kenshin (1996) episodes 1-62
steps.note: Covers the essential Tokyo + Kyoto material.

steps.title: Reflection OVA
steps.note: Anime-original and controversial as an ending.

franchises.name: A Certain Magical Index / Railgun
franchises.summary: The franchise overlaps in time. For a first watch, a block order is easier and preserves reveals better than an obsessive scene-by-scene chronology.

steps.title: A Certain Scientific Railgun S
steps.note: Its Sisters arc gives the most detailed version of events that overlap Index.
